stem:
Meher looks at the diagram. It shows the front, top, and side views of one solid.

Which claim correctly decides how to identify the solid from those views?

options.text: Use the front, top, and side views together; one projection alone is not enough.
Match the solid from the front view alone.
Having named the solid is what creates the three views.
Also treat any single corner sketch as enough under the same three-view rule.

teacher.key_rationale: A single projection is not unique, so front, top, and side views together identify the solid. Front alone, reversing cause, or stretching to one corner sketch miss that need.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source cuboid net as labelled front, top, and side orthographic views of an L-shaped solid.
